1-2-3: Someone with something hypnotic and pleasant about them, who instantly calms even people in the middle of a fight.
A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.
4-5-6: Someone who reaches heights others don't dare to, and when they heat up, their warmth is powerful enough to burn.
Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.
7-8-9: Someone who looks guarded and protected on the outside, but when they fire, their words pierce even the thickest barriers.
The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.
10-11-12: A hardworking, quiet person who gathers something small and sweet every day and makes sure to bring it home for everyone.
It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.
13-14-15: Someone with several stingers ready, who isn't satisfied with one: confront them and they jab again and again.
It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.
16-17-18: A very fast person always looking for the next opportunity, and when they grab it, their grip is frightening.
This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.
19-20: Someone who adapts to any environment, even one not built for them, and finds a way to get what they need there.
Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.
21-22: A seasoned person who has seen a lot, and the second they sense danger, they're already far away and above it all.
A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.
23-24: Someone with an intimidating look that people have been trying to decode for years, still discovering more and more patterns in them.
The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.
27-28: Someone who climbs up on their own to get something good, then shares it with those waiting below who can't climb yet.
It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.
29-30-31: Someone all prickly on the outside, but when the little ones are close, they disarm every sting so they feel safe.
It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.
32-33-34: Someone proud of their strength, who enters every confrontation with fire and force and uses everything they have to break any barrier.
Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.
37-38: Someone with an impressive, glittering presence, said to hold a deep, quiet power kept for a very long time.
The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.
41-42-169: Someone who turned what they had into one more tool for moving forward, and can maneuver fast even in the most crowded places without slowing down.
Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.
43-44-45: Someone who grows sharper the more they bloom and stand out, and sometimes their head is too heavy to carry.
The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
43-44-182: Someone who loves gathering with others and dancing, as if their joy could bring out the sun.
Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.
46-47: Someone who looks as if something bigger than them is running them, and without it they simply stay still.
Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.
48-49: Someone hard to shake off once you've touched them, who leaves something prickly on anyone who comes near.
The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.
50-51: Someone who digs to a depth no one reaches, and no one really knows what goes on with them down there.
These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.
52-53: A refined, elegant person who looks down with mutual disdain on anyone who behaves crudely, even someone very close.
Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.
54-55: A strong, trained person who gets through even the stormiest periods with ease, battling every wave until it passes.
Its body is strong, and it has webbing on its hands and feet. Golduck can swim easily through rough seas, clawing its way through the high waves.
56-57-979: Someone who keeps a quiet, deep anger in their heart, and when they finally let it out, it shakes the other side to its foundations.
It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.
58-59: A powerful, fiery person who moves lightly despite their size, leading opponents astray as if in a dance.
Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.
60-61-62: Someone at home both in the water and in the ring, who uses a well-trained body to land powerful blows.
Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.
60-61-186: Someone whose voice carries far, and whose deep, menacing side is exactly what draws people to them.
The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.
63-64-65: Someone whose head grows heavier every year, and right there, in the weight of their thoughts, lies all their power.
The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.
66-67-68: Someone who arrives at close combat with twice the hands, attacking and defending at once, able to overwhelm the other side in a moment.
In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.
69-70-71: Someone who draws people in with sweetness, and whoever gets pulled inside is swallowed whole, with nothing left of them.
Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.
72-73: Someone with many far-reaching arms, each with a sting. Be careful when they reach out a hand.
It has 80 tentacles, each with a venomous tip. These tentacles are also extendible, lengthening when Tentacruel attempts to catch prey. Use caution.
74-75-76: Someone who sheds a hard layer every year, and what they leave behind becomes soil that grows things for others.
The rocklike shell is shed each year. The cast-off shell then crumbles, reverting to a mass of soil, which can be spread across fields to promote crop growth.
77-78: A fast, burning person who crosses huge distances in a short time and leaves a trail of fire behind.
Fiery mane aglow, Rapidash darts like an arrow across the land. This prodigiously swift creature can traverse the vast region of Hisui in a day and a half.
79-80: Someone something once clung to and shook them until they stood upright, and if it lets go, they'll go back to who they were.
Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.
79-199: Someone who can solve any problem brought to them, but no one manages to understand what they're saying.
Slowking can solve any problem presented to it, but no one can understand a thing Slowking says.
81-82-462: Someone changed from within by a special force field around them, who keeps transmitting strange signals to somewhere beyond.
I theorize that a special magnetic field influenced this Pokémon, changing its molecular structure and causing it to evolve. It emits strange radio waves toward space from its antenna.
84-85: Someone whose head splits in so many directions they're almost a different person, and who still runs faster than anyone in open space.
One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.
86-87: A bright, quiet person whom the cold doesn't hurt at all, swimming powerfully even in the most frozen conditions.
Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.
88-89: Someone whose presence is unbearably heavy for others, though they themselves stopped feeling it long ago.
Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.
90-91: Someone who, once closed, can't be opened by any force, not even by those stronger than them.
Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.
92-93-94: Someone who slips into your shadow and tries to steal something of your life. If your shadow starts laughing, look for a protective charm.
Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!
95-208: Someone who went through a strange change in life and grew such a hard shell that nothing leaves even a scratch on them anymore.
This Pokémon evolved through use of a strange item. Its body is coated with steel powder and notably hard—not even diamond can leave so much as a scratch.
96-97: Someone whose direct gaze is best avoided, because they know how to lull you to sleep and lead you wherever they want.
Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.
98-99: Someone with one huge strength that decides every struggle, but in daily life it mostly gets in their way.
Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.
100-101: Someone who looks round and innocent from the outside, but when annoyed, releases the power of twenty lightning bolts.
The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
102-103: Someone who produces tremendous brainpower when all their parts work together, but on a gray day is simply slow.
When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.
104-105: Someone who carries the one they lost as part of themselves, and since the loss, something in them has grown hard and aggressive.
When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.
108-463: Someone whose words reach very far, way beyond their size, and what they leave behind burns.
Its tongue can extend and contract freely, and it is capable of reaching lengths over 10 times Lickilicky's height. Beware of the saliva, as it contains corrosive elements.
109-110: Someone who may not hold the most air, but what they put out is sharper and more toxic than anyone like them.
It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.
111-112-464: Someone a strange change gave such hard skin that even the most perfect blow leaves no mark.
This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.
114-465: Someone who looks like a tangled, wild bush, but when they reach out their arms, they catch and wrap up everything that comes near.
Draped with long vines, it resembles a shrub in appearance. It swings bundles of vines as though they were arms, wrapping them around prey to ensnare them.
115: Someone who raises and protects even those who aren't theirs, giving a home to kids who've lost their way.
There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.
116-117-230: Someone whose shed layers are so brilliant they're given as gifts to kings.
Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they’ve been given to royalty as gifts.
118-119: Someone who stubbornly drills and builds a safe place so that what's dear to them won't be swept away by the current.
Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.
120-121: Someone who moves forward by spinning fast around themselves, soaking up every little detail along the way.
Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.
123-212: Someone who changed in an extraordinary way, and the shell they built for themselves is stronger than steel.
Evolved by way of a curious item. The shell covering its body has been shown to be stronger than forged steel.
123-900: A violent, rough person who mows down everything in front of them, protected by hard armor, and whoever meets them had better run.
A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.
127: Someone who, once they grab hold of something, either breaks it in two or throws it far away.
This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.
128: Someone with an explosive temper who won't let anyone climb on their back or steer them.
The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.
129-130: Someone whose stories are already bigger than they are: legends of huge destruction, and inside, a burning power no one appreciated.
I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.
131: Someone who gets through even the coldest periods with ease, and whoever touches them feels a light coolness, not cold.
Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.
132: Someone who, when they meet someone like them, works especially hard to be exactly like them, only faster.
When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.
133-134: Someone who blends into their surroundings until they can't be seen, and about whom the legends were born.
Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.
133-135: Someone whose hair all turns into sharp spikes when they're angry, and you can hear electricity in the air when they breathe.
Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.
133-136: Someone with an inner flame that every breath only fuels, until it burns with tremendous force.
Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
133-196: Someone with a hidden power that lets them foresee what will happen and even what people are thinking, and who fills with energy in the sun.
Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.
133-197: Someone most awake and active in the small hours of the night, who sees in the deepest dark what others miss.
It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.
133-470: Someone soft and green inside, almost plant-like, but when they strike, their sharpness beats any blade.
Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.
133-471: Someone who can cool themselves in a moment, and out of that cold creates beautiful sparkles around them when they dance.
Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.
133-700: Someone with a calming aura who wraps themselves around people who are arguing and instantly brings back the quiet.
It emits a soothing aura from its ribbon-shaped organs. It wraps these appendages around quarrelers to instantly restore calm to the situation.
137-233-474: Someone a strange change made much stronger in attack, but just as much stranger too, and that's worrying.
A curious item induced this evolution. The Pokémon's offensive capabilities have greatly increased, but the strangeness of its behavior has magnified in equal measure. This worries me.
138-139: Someone with power that can crush rock, but who can only use it on whoever comes close enough to be in range.
Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.
140-141: An aggressive, independent person who ruled their arena and then vanished, with no one knowing why their road ended.
The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.
142: Someone with teeth as sharp as a saw, able to tear through even someone everyone thinks is impenetrable.
Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.
147-148-149: Someone who became a symbol leading others on the open sea, and like a figurehead on a ship's bow, everyone wants them at the front.
This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.
152-153-154: Someone whose presence soothes emotions, and who in an argument radiates even more calm to neutralize the other side's heat.
The fragrance of Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.
155-156-157: Someone said to purify lost souls with their fire and see them on their way, as if built by a holy place.
Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.
158-159-160: Someone threatening just by opening their mouth, and when they attack, they charge forward at amazing speed.
Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.
161-162: A thin, flexible person who, when attacked, slips through any narrow gap and disappears, even with short steps.
Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.
163-164: Someone who, when they need to think, flips their point of view completely, and that's what sharpens them.
When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.
165-166: Someone who passes by at night scattering sparkles, and it's said that whoever they stick to will have good things happen.
It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.
167-168: Someone who weaves a web to catch what they want, and when night falls, comes out of it to hunt aggressively.
It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.
170-171: Someone who blinds the other side with a strong light, and right in that moment of confusion lands the blow.
This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.
172-25-26: A relatively small person whose single burst contains such power that it can knock out even giants.
It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.
173-35-36: Someone who on quiet nights listens to the voices of a distant family and longs for a home far from here.
Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
174-39-40: Someone very proud of how they look, especially one small detail that in their eyes is simply perfect.
It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.
175-176-468: A rare person almost no one sees, who appears only when there is quiet and peace around them.
Scant few have ever sighted this Pokémon. After studying what literature remains, I am certain Togekiss will reveal itself when peace reigns in the land.
177-178: A strange person who sees both the past and the future, and can stare all day in one direction without moving.
This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.
179-180-181: Someone who glows strong and steady, and has been a lighthouse for years to anyone looking for the way.
Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.
187-188-189: Someone carried on warm winds to distant lands, who lands and returns to the ground when the atmosphere cools.
Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.
190-424: Someone who strengthens bonds by linking arms with others in a circle, and sometimes takes strangers into it too.
To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.
191-192: Someone who turns sunlight into energy, very active when it's warm and pleasant, and who stops the moment the sun sets.
Sunflora converts solar energy into nutrition. It moves around actively in the daytime when it is warm. It stops moving as soon as the sun goes down for the night.
193-469: A violent, energy-saving person who aims only at the most vulnerable points, and whoever tames them needs tremendous courage.
Extremely violent. When hunting, it wastes none of its energy, aiming only for prey's most vulnerable spots. Any who manage to tame this Pokémon must be of incredible bravery.
194-195: A slippery person who bumps their head on every obstacle along the way, and doesn't seem bothered by it at all.
Its body is always slimy. It often bangs its head on the river bottom as it swims but seems not to care.
198-430: Someone whose single call instantly brings a whole flock, and then it seems a curtain of night has fallen on everyone.
One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.
200-429: Someone whose words guard against bad luck, and people like to invite them home. But anger them, and trouble comes.
The incantations Mismagius chants can ward against misfortune, so a custom exists of inviting it into one's home. Incur the Pokémon's displeasure, however, and disaster will surely ensue.
201: Someone so strange it's hard to believe they're real, and whoever tries to explain them isn't taken seriously by anyone.
It is hard to believe these strangely shaped Pokémon are truly living creatures. I've pointed out that the species' many forms resemble writing from other lands; no one will take me seriously.
203-981: Someone with an extra side that guards their back, so they can charge forward without fear.
The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.
204-205: Someone completely closed inside themselves, who opens only for a brief moment, so brief that no one has ever seen what's inside.
In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.
206-982: Someone who protects their home by taking a deep breath and then letting it all out at once with a force that drives everyone away.
It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.
207-472: Someone who glides in total silence in the dark, strikes at exactly the right spot, and seems satisfied only when nothing is left.
It glides soundlessly on pitch-black wings and sinks sharp fangs into the throat of its prey. It takes on a look of satisfaction once it has entirely drained its prey of blood.
209-210: Someone who looks tough and menacing, but is actually shy and sensitive, and not at all suited to be anyone's guard.
Although it’s popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it’s totally incompetent as a watchdog.
213: Someone who keeps good things inside for a long time, until they ripen into something thick and rich.
The berries stored in its vaselike shell eventually become a thick, pulpy juice.
214: Someone with unrivaled strength, able to lift and toss several trained people at once.
This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.
215-461: Someone who works in a pack under a leader, and as they grew, their cunning sharpened as if their brain had evolved.
This species corners prey as a pack, under the guidance of a leader. Weavile displays increased cunning, leading me to speculate that its evolution caused further brain development.
216-217-901: Someone whose muddy upbringing shaped a bulky, strong body and a new ability to do with it as they please.
I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.
218-219: Someone so fiery that every drop that touches them instantly turns to steam, wrapping everything around in fog.

Magcargo’s body temperature is approximately 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Water is vaporized on contact. If this Pokémon is caught in the rain, the raindrops instantly turn into steam, cloaking the area in a thick fog.
220-221-473: Someone who reached their peak in the coldest period, when the cold actually awakened hidden powers in them.
This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.
223-224: Someone who changed so much that for a long time no one believed they were the same person they once were.
While Octillery still shoots water from its mouth, the drastic anatomical difference between it and Remoraid meant that for a long time, no one believed the former evolved from the latter.
225: A generous person who shares their food with everyone, and so is always looking for more.
It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it’s always scrounging around for more food.
227: Someone for whom even what they shed becomes a weapon, which is why they're a symbol of honor and status.
People fashion swords from Skarmory’s shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.
228-229: Someone recognized by their chilling howl, whom people once feared as if they were death itself.
Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.
231-232: Someone whose strength could destroy a whole house, but who uses it to clear obstacles from other people's way.
If Donphan were to tackle with its hard body, even a house could be destroyed. Using its massive strength, the Pokémon helps clear rock and mud slides that block mountain trails.
234-899: Someone who puts up invisible barriers around themselves, but what they shed warms others in winter.
The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.
235: Someone who creates their own symbols and works, and has fans willing to pay a fortune for them.
It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.
236-106: Someone who reaches very far when needed, and can hit even those who think they're safe at a distance.
The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.
236-107: Someone whose blows cut through the air, but who needs a break after three minutes of confrontation.
Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.
236-237: Someone who confuses the other side by standing on their head, and then pulls out their impressive moves.
After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent’s timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.
238-124: Someone with a beautiful, gentle voice who has even gathered a crowd of fans around them.
The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.
239-125-466: Someone who releases more energy the faster their heart beats, up to tremendous power.
Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.
240-126-467: Someone a strange change made especially fiery, whose shots can melt even the hardest things.
Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.
241: Someone who has to give of what they have every day or they get sick, and what they give changes with the seasons.
This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.
246-247-248: Someone whose every step shakes the surroundings, until even big mountains crumble and change shape.
The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.
252-253-254: Someone who carries on their back what revives others, and raises everyone around them with love and patience.
Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.
255-256-257: Someone with strong legs who can jump over a building in one leap, and whatever they hit stays scorched.
Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon’s blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.
258-259-260: Someone who senses a storm coming from subtle changes in the sounds around them, and builds a shelter before it arrives.
Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.
261-262: Someone who acts in a pack and remembers well where they came from, so they obey only someone who has proven truly better.
Mightyena travel and act as a pack in the wild. The memory of its life in the wild compels the Pokémon to obey only those Trainers that it recognizes to possess superior skill.
265-266-267: A wonderfully colorful, beautiful person, but greedy too, who drives others away to keep what they love most for themselves.
A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.
265-268-269: Someone drawn to light on dark nights, and hard to keep away because they scatter toxic things around them.
Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.
270-271-272: Someone who starts moving to the beat when they hear happy music, and that's how their power grows.
If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.
273-274-275: Someone who lives quietly, far from the center, and it's said that with one movement they can bring a cool breeze to the whole room.
It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.
276-277: Someone very particular about their appearance, and when they meet someone like them, they take care of each other.
Swellow is very conscientious about the upkeep of its glossy wings. Once two Swellow are gathered, they diligently take care of cleaning each other’s wings.
278-279: Someone who skims across the surface, gathering everything needed along the way and bringing it to whoever is waiting.
Skimming the water’s surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.
280-281-282: Someone devoted to protecting the ones they love, ready to risk themselves for them without a second thought.
It will dedicate itself to defending a master it has come to adore. Its pure white dress, reminiscent of those worn by ladies of nobility, is the dress of one who is willing to risk their life.
280-281-475: Someone whose sharpness beats the finest tools, who learned everything alone, and whose skill is still astonishing.
The blades extending from its elbows are sharper than the finest swords. Its swordsmanship, albeit self-taught, is astonishingly impressive.
283-284: Someone who absorbs everything from their surroundings, and on rainy days simply waits quietly somewhere sheltered until it passes.
Its thin, winglike antennae are highly absorbent. It waits out rainy days in tree hollows.
285-286: Someone whose apparent gift turns out to be toxic, and even a small taste of it turns your stomach.
The seeds ringing Breloom’s tail are made of hardened toxic spores. It is horrible to eat the seeds. Just taking a bite of this Pokémon’s seed will cause your stomach to rumble.
287-288-289: Someone who doesn't get up from their spot, but eats everything within reach, until an empty circle is left around them.
Wherever Slaking live, rings of over a yard in diameter appear in grassy fields. They are made by the Pokémon as it eats all the grass within reach while lying prone on the ground.
290-291: Someone so fast it's said they can help you dodge any blow, and who mostly loves to sip the sweet stuff.
This Pokémon is so quick, it is said to be able to avoid any attack. It loves to feed on tree sap.
290-292: A strange person who seems to move without doing anything, with a hollow shell outside and no sign of life inside.
A strange Pokémon—it flies without moving its wings, has a hollow shell for a body, and does not breathe.
293-294-295: Someone who can do much more than shout, communicating with those close to them through their whole range of voices.
This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it’ll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.
296-297: Someone who reminds us that size isn't everything: there are small ones who move nimbly and use their moves with skill.
Hariyama that are big and fat aren’t necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.
298-183-184: A protective person who wraps those younger than them in gentle protection, so they can play without worry.
These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.
299-476: Someone with a strong magnetic pull, who shapes what's drawn to them into a hard tool to strike with.
It is able to emit powerful magnetism, allowing it control over the iron sand that forms its luscious mustache. Using this iron sand, Probopass forms hard stones with which it smites its prey.
300-301: Someone who sleeps wherever they like with no fixed home, and when someone approaches, doesn't fight, just gets up and moves.
Delcatty sleeps anywhere it wants without keeping a permanent nest. If other Pokémon approach it as it sleeps, this Pokémon will never fight—it will just move away somewhere else.
302: Someone who feeds on precious things, and whose eyes sparkle like jewels in the dark.
It feeds on gemstone crystals. In darkness, its eyes sparkle with the glitter of jewels.
303: Someone with huge steel jaws hidden behind a cute face, which used to be a different part of them.
It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.
304-305-306: Someone kings wanted to look like, hoping a little of their power would rub off on them.
Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon’s strength.
307-308: Someone who developed a sixth sense through meditation and can sit a whole month with themselves without eating.
Through the power of meditation, Medicham developed its sixth sense. It gained the ability to use psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon is known to meditate for a whole month without eating.
309-310: Someone who rarely appears in front of people, and is said to build their home exactly where lightning struck.
It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.
311: Someone who cheers on their partner with their whole body and every spark, and cries out loud if the partner loses.
When Plusle is cheering on its partner, it flashes with electric sparks from all over its body. If its partner loses, this Pokémon cries loudly.
312: Someone who loves cheering on their partner, and the deeper the partner's trouble, the harder they try.
Minun loves to cheer on its partner in battle. It gives off sparks from its body while it is doing so. If its partner is in trouble, this Pokémon gives off increasing amounts of sparks.
313: Someone who glows and draws shapes in the night sky with their friends, and is strongly drawn to one particular sweet scent.
Volbeat’s tail glows like a lightbulb. With other Volbeat, it uses its tail to draw geometric shapes in the night sky. This Pokémon loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.
314: Someone who leads others in a shared creation, and the more complex the creation, the more respected they are.
Illumise leads a flight of illuminated Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. This Pokémon is said to earn greater respect from its peers by composing more complex designs in the sky.
316-317: Someone who chews nothing and just swallows everything whole, and almost anything fits into their gaping mouth.
Swalot has no teeth, so what it eats, it swallows whole, no matter what. Its cavernous mouth yawns widely. An automobile tire could easily fit inside this Pokémon’s mouth.
318-319: Someone known as the bully of the place, who attacks anyone who enters their territory, no exceptions.
This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sea. Any ship entering the waters Sharpedo calls home will be attacked—no exceptions.
320-321: Someone whose whole popularity comes from their huge size, and people come from afar just to see them.
Its immense size is the reason for its popularity. Wailord watching is a favorite sightseeing activity in various parts of the world.
322-323: Someone something in their bones changed, creating fiery reservoirs inside, and who seems to erupt often when angry.
The humps on Camerupt’s back are formed by a transformation of its bones. They sometimes blast out molten magma. This Pokémon apparently erupts often when it is enraged.
324: Someone who finds their place in the very places others abandoned, digging in them nonstop in search of what will feed them.
You find abandoned coal mines full of them. They dig tirelessly in search of coal.
325-326: Someone who draws wondrous powers from something precious they carry, and dances oddly while using them.
Grumpig uses the black pearls on its body to wield its fantastic powers. When it is doing so, it dances bizarrely. This Pokémon’s black pearls are valuable as works of art.
327: Someone with no one else like them, whose stumbling steps actually help them dodge every blow.
Each Spinda’s spot pattern is different. With its stumbling movements, it evades opponents’ attacks brilliantly!
328-329-330: Someone called the spirit of the desert, because when they move it sounds like singing.
It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.
331-332: Someone who patiently follows whoever is tired, waiting for the moment they can't move anymore.

If a traveler is going through a desert in the thick of night, Cacturne will follow in a ragtag group. The Pokémon are biding their time, waiting for the traveler to tire and become incapable of moving.
333-334: Someone with a gentle temper, but if provoked, they warn with a sharp shriek and then attack without mercy.
This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it’s provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.
335: Someone usually low and quiet, but when angry they rise up and draw their claws, and they have an old, bitter rivalry.
Zangoose usually stays on all fours, but when angered, it gets up on its hind legs and extends its claws. This Pokémon shares a bitter rivalry with Seviper that dates back over generations.
336: Someone whose sharp tongue both cuts and poisons, and who won't let go of an ancient feud.
Seviper’s swordlike tail serves two purposes—it slashes foes and douses them with secreted poison. This Pokémon will not give up its long-running blood feud with Zangoose.
337: Someone who arrived as if fallen from the sky, and one look from them can put whoever faces them to sleep.
It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.
338: Someone who draws their power from the sun, especially strong during the day, and who glows when they spin.
Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.
339-340: Someone who shakes the ground to startle everyone around, and people have mistaken them for the cause of every tremor.
Strikes its caudal fin against the swamp bed to shake the ground and startle its prey. It will then swallow the fleeing prey whole. People mistook this behavior as the cause of earthquakes.
341-342: A rough person who loves a confrontation and pounces on anyone who comes near their territory.
A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.
343-344: Someone who seems made from the dolls of ancient people, floating from place to place by the power of thought alone.
It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.
345-346: Someone who, once they catch something, absorbs it completely and takes everything it has.
Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.
347-348: Someone who lives on land but swims excellently, and dives deep when they want to get something.
Though it lives on land, it’s also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.
349-350: Someone whose beauty, at a single glance, calms every hostile feeling in you.
It’s said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you’re feeling.
351: Someone who changes with the weather, and the stormier the conditions, the stormier their temper.
Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform’s disposition!
352: Someone who changes color to blend in, and also when their mood changes. The darker they get, the healthier they are.
Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.
353-354: Someone born of resentment at being thrown away, and it's said that if treated kindly, they'll calm down and become what they were.
Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.
355-356-477: Someone who comes to those whose road has ended and escorts them onward, and sometimes, rarely, makes a mistake and takes someone too early.
Comes to those whose lives have come to an end and escorts their souls to the afterlife. Known to mistakenly take the souls of those who yet have life left in them, albeit rarely.
357: Someone around whom good things grow for others to enjoy, and whom people in warm places happily raise.
Bunches of delicious fruit grow around its neck. In warm areas, many ranches raise Tropius.
359: Someone who senses danger before anyone else, so people mistakenly thought they were the one who brought it.
Because of this Pokémon’s ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.
360-202: Someone who hides their dark side and lives quietly in the shadows, and never attacks first.
To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.
361-362: Someone who wraps themselves in armor colder and harder than steel, and freezes whoever faces them with one breath.
It covers its body with an armor of ice harder than steel. Uses its breath to freeze prey, which it then devours as if they were frozen desserts.
361-478: Someone who carries an old, cold grudge inside, and legends tell of curses they cast on those who behave badly.
A Pokémon inhabited by the soul of a woman who died bearing a grudge in the snowy mountains. Legends of Froslass placing deathly curses on misbehaving men send shivers down my spine.
363-364-365: Someone strong enough to break any ice, and if something in them breaks, it grows back by next year.
Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.
366-367: Someone who lives in the depths, and tradition says that when they rise to the surface, something bad is about to happen.
Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.
366-368: Someone who takes what they need from others, and what's left of them becomes food for others.
It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.
369: Someone who hasn't changed in forever, which is why they're called a living fossil.
This Pokémon was discovered during deep-sea exploration. Its appearance hasn’t changed in 100,000,000 years, so it’s called a living fossil.
370: Someone who builds a home in a warm, colorful place, and especially loves sleeping in someone else's arms.
Luvdisc makes its home in coral reefs in warm seas. It especially likes sleeping in the space between Corsola’s branches.
371-372-373: Someone who usually floats around happy and in high spirits, but when something angers them, becomes an unstoppable threat.
While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.
374-375-376: Someone created from the merging of two, who beats rivals mostly thanks to a brain that works like a supercomputer.
Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.
387-388-389: A wonderfully big, strong person you could build a whole garden around, who wanders far in search of clean water.
This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.
390-391-392: A tall, tough person with a dazzling presence, who wraps themselves in fire and fights as if dancing.
A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.
393-394-395: Someone revered since ancient times as the lord of the waves, whose sharp movements match the finest tools.
Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.
396-397-398: Someone who left the pack once strong enough to survive alone, and can now carry even the heaviest along.
It has left the flock, having gained strength enough to survive on its own. The astounding force with which Staraptor flies through the air allows it to carry away large, burly targets.
399-400: Someone who builds dams to make a home, and nothing gets through to them, but next to them it's always warm.
Bibarel fur repels water and is also a fantastic material for heat retention. These Pokémon create dams on rivers to live in.
401-402: Someone who makes a melody all their own, different from anyone else's, and it's worth the effort to find their song.
It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.
403-404-405: Someone who leads their group, and it's said that when their eyes shine, they see through anything.
They form packs, each having one male as leader. Legends say that when Luxray's two eyes shimmer with gold, the Pokémon can see through anything.
406-315-407: Someone holding a beautiful bouquet in each hand, with thorny, poisonous whips hidden inside. They move gracefully, then lash out without mercy.
Hidden within the bouquet on each hand are thorned whips loaded with virulent poison. Roserade moves gracefully as it corners its prey and mercilessly lashes them with its whips.
408-409: Someone almost nothing is known about, but with their beautiful, hard head they can topple huge trees.
Very little is known about its biology. Can knock down massive trees by smashing its beautiful, pearl-like crown against them.
410-411: Someone with a diamond-hard face that steadily protects them, and still, much about them remains unknown.
Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.
412-413: Someone for whom what wrapped them in their youth became part of their body, and they never take it off.
When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon’s body. The cloak is never shed.
412-414: Someone who loves sweet things, but for some reason is hardly ever seen where they grow.
Scatters steel-colored scales as it flaps its wings. Despite being observed feeding primarily on the nectar of flowers, Mothim is not often seen around flower gardens.
415-416: Someone who runs everyone and orders them to build their home, and whoever dares to sneak in ends up finished there.
Commands its subjects to build its hive. It will dispatch any interlopers who dare sneak into its nest and use them as nourishment for itself.
417: Someone mostly calm, but still dangerous to anyone who touches them in the wrong places.
A species related to the Pikachu line. Though Pachirisu is a calm Pokémon, it still presents a danger should one touch its electrified tail or cheeks.
418-419: Someone with something that keeps them afloat even in the stormiest times, seen wandering around the small villages.
Has a long, rather splendid flotation sac, which prevents Floatzel from drowning even in stormy seas. One might glimpse this species around fishing hamlets from time to time.
420-421: Someone who barely moves, yet people of all kinds gather around them, drawn to something they radiate.
Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim's folded petals.
422-423: Someone content with what's around them, but when they meet someone similar in a different color, a fierce battle begins.
Eats beach sand for nourishment. Should one Gastrodon encounter another of a different color, a fierce battle will inevitably ensue.
425-426: Someone who drifts quietly at dusk, with a passing sadness that moves people to write poems about them.
It drifts along at dusk, perfectly silent. Its transient, melancholy aspect touches some people deeply—every so often, one will come upon a song or poem devoted to Drifblim.
427-428: Someone warm and pleasant but amazingly light, who kicks like a karate champion when someone needs to be kept away.
Its fur is warm and yet remarkably light. This Pokémon kicks as though it were a master of karate, driving back its opponents with ease.
431-432: A cheeky person hard to tame, but people admire them for their stunning looks.
Though impudent and difficult to tame, Purugly enjoys great popularity due to its fur, the beauty of which surpasses even velveteen.
433-358: Someone who amplifies inside them the faintest sound they heard, until they can knock down even someone bigger.
Can emit waves of air powerful enough to knock out prey taller than itself. I hypothesize that it amplifies the faint sound of wind within its body.
434-435: Someone who uses something smelly to win, and sometimes even they can't stand the smell and leave what they gained.
Sprays a poisonous fluid to take down prey. Sometimes, unable to stomach the stench of its own fluid, it leaves the bested prey uneaten.
436-437: Someone whose voice sounds like a bell, and some believe they open doors to another world. Revered almost like a god.
Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.
438-185: Someone who pretends to be something else, but can't fool even kids, and is especially afraid of one particular thing.
Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.
440-113-242: A kind-hearted person who looks after anyone sick until they recover, and what they give others brings them luck.
A kindhearted Pokémon that will care for any sick person or Pokémon until their health improves. The eggs it lays are delicious and bring good fortune to those who eat them.
441: A talented mimic who can repeat everything said, and it's said the old ones understand the meaning of the words too.
A versatile performer skilled in the imitation of human speech. It is said that older, more experienced Chatot can even understand the meaning of the words they mimic.
442: Someone who affects their surroundings only with negative thoughts, and seems like a collection of many bad spirits together.
It lays curses by thinking wicked thoughts. Writings tell that this Pokémon was born out of the assembly of five score and eight malevolent spirits.
443-444-445: Someone who crosses the sky at dazzling speed, a stunning sight, but there's something wild in them, and in the field you should be very careful.
Soars across the heavens at blinding speed—a magnificent sight! It has a feral disposition. Utmost caution is required if one meets a Garchomp out in the wilds.
446-143: Someone who arrives without warning and devours everything gathered, long considered one of the great disasters.
This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.
447-448: A noble-looking person who radiates energy and knows how to aim it precisely, and senses even those far away.
A most gallant-looking creature. It emits energy waves and controls them with precision, using them to sense even faraway beings. I have given the name ”aura” to this power.
449-450: A hot-tempered person who erupts easily, raises a sandstorm that breaks the other side's spirit, and only then attacks.
Short-tempered and easily moved to violence. It whips up whirlwinds of sand to crush its foes' spirits, then goes in for the attack.
451-452: Someone with a rough, wild temper, huge strength and armor that swords bounce off, who rampages and leaves destruction behind.
Has a brutish, ferocious temperament. With immense strength and a sturdy shell off which swords will bounce, it rampages about and wreaks havoc.
453-454: Someone whose coating is poisonous, but if diluted patiently and combined right, it becomes medicine.
Its crimson claws contain a virulent toxin. This toxin can be made into a tonic by diluting it, mixing it with several types of wild grass, and boiling it down over two days.
455: Someone who looks like a calm plant, but is actually a wild glutton who attacks with a wide-open mouth.
Though this is a plant Pokémon, it has a gluttonous and unruly temperament. Carnivine attacks its prey with its cavernous maw wide open.
456-457: Someone who uses their shine to get what they want, and the sight of them and their friends at night is breathtaking, like stars.
Uses its gleaming fins to hunt its prey. The view of Lumineon schooling near the surface of the sea at night is breathtaking— it's as though there were shining stars right there.
458-226: A calm, gentle person who glides gracefully, and when they gather speed they leap so high people think they're someone else.
This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.
459-460: A strong person who can easily split huge rocks, but dislikes company and chooses to live quietly, far away, playing in the snow.
A powerful Pokémon that can split huge boulders with ease. Dislikes associating with others and chooses to live quietly deep within the mountains, playing with the snow.
479: A strange person who looks like a wandering spark, and is worth watching out for, because they're both clever and mischievous.
This bizarre Pokémon appears to be a will-o'-the-wisp powered by electricity. Be wary, as Rotom is both smart and mischievous.
495-496-497: Someone who can stop the other side with just a look, absorbing light from outside and amplifying it within.
It can stop its opponents’ movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.
498-499-500: Someone who masters fast, powerful moves, and whose fire simply grows on their face.
It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.
501-502-503: A hard-hearted, quick-handed person whose blows crash on the other side like waves that never stop.
Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon's evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.
504-505: Someone who stands guard, and the moment they see an enemy, they rise up and spit what they'd been saving at them.
When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.
506-507-508: Someone very proud of their impressive mustache, and in their crowd, mustache length decides your status.
Stoutland is immensely proud of its impressive moustache. It’s said that moustache length is what determines social standing among this species.
509-510: Someone who sneaks up from behind without a sound and fights for their territory against a cunning rival.
This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.
511-512: Someone with a bad temper who fights with wild movements, and what grows on their head is very bitter.
Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.
513-514: Someone who starts sparking and heating up when excited, and for some reason is crazy about sweets.
When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.
515-516: Someone who prefers a clean environment, and when they run empty, knows exactly how to refill themselves.
It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.
517-518: Someone who dreams and dozes all the time, and it's best not to come near when they wake up, because then they're terribly grumpy.
It drowses and dreams all the time. It’s best to leave it be if it’s just woken up, as it’s a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.
519-520-521: A wise and very proud person, and whoever manages to be at their side immediately gains attention and respect.
This Pokémon is intelligent and intensely proud. People will sit up and take notice if you become the Trainer of one.
522-523: Someone with lightning moves, and when they run at full speed, an echo of thunder rolls after them.
They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.
524-525-526: Someone with the power to toss a truck, but with one limit: they can only use it when the sun is out.
Although its energy blasts can blow away a dump truck, they have a limitation— they can only be fired when the sun is out.
527-528: Someone something about whose looks is considered a sign of luck, seen in some places as a charm.
The auspicious shape of this Pokémon’s nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.
529-530: Someone called the king of drills, who bores through every obstacle at dizzying speed.
Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.
531: A good-hearted person who with a single touch can understand what others feel and how they are.
This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.
532-533-534: Someone who, when giving it their all, throws aside their heavy work tools and jumps in barehanded.
When going all out, this Pokémon throws aside its concrete pillars and leaps at opponents to pummel them with its fists.
535-536-537: Someone older people especially love, because what comes out of them does them good, like a massage.
This Pokémon is popular among the elderly, who say the vibrations of its lumps are great for massages.
538: Someone who trains in a small group, and when someone can't keep up, they take off their belt and leave.
They train in groups of five. Any member that can’t keep up will discard its belt and leave the group.
539: Someone who trained to the limit, and one punch of theirs can split even the ocean.
The karate chops of a Sawk that’s trained itself to the limit can cleave the ocean itself.
540-541-542: Someone who makes sure to warm and wrap whoever is smaller than them, with whatever is around.
It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.
543-544-545: Someone who fights hard for their territory, and at the end of the struggle the winner swallows the loser.
Scolipede engage in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch. At the end of one of these battles, the victor makes a meal of the loser.
546-547: Someone who just keeps growing softer as long as they're in the sun, and when too much builds up, simply shakes it off and scatters it.
As long as this Pokémon bathes in sunlight, its cotton keeps growing. If too much cotton fluff builds up, Whimsicott tears it off and scatters it.
548-549: Someone whose hard road built them strong legs, and whose scent encourages everyone around them.
I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.
551-552-553: A very aggressive person, but patient enough to hide for days and wait for the right moment.
While terribly aggressive, Krookodile also has the patience to stay hidden under sand for days, lying in wait for prey.
554-555: Someone whose power rises as their fire heats up, to extreme temperatures.
This Pokémon’s power level rises along with the temperature of its fire, which can reach 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit.
556: Someone who once a year scatters what they grew, and it's so nourishing it's a treasure in a place with nothing.
Once each year, this Pokémon scatters its seeds. They’re jam-packed with nutrients, making them a precious food source out in the desert.
557-558: Someone whose thick tools are their best weapon, strong enough to crack even the hardest armor.
Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They’re mighty enough to crack Rhyperior’s carapace.
559-560: Someone known mostly as an aggressive bully, but who cares deeply about family, friends and territory.
While mostly known for having the temperament of an aggressive ruffian, this Pokémon takes very good care of its family, friends, and territory.
561: Someone around whom remains of an ancient, buried world suddenly come to light.
A discovery was made in the desert where Sigilyph fly. The ruins of what may have been an ancient city were found beneath the sands.
562-563: Someone who appears in ancient paintings as a symbol of the wealth and status of those who were once on top.
There are many depictions of Cofagrigus decorating ancient tombs. They’re symbols of the wealth that kings of bygone eras had.
564-565: Someone who leaves their comfort zone to get what they want, even if outside they move more slowly.
This Pokémon emerges from the water in search of prey despite the fact that it moves more slowly on land.
566-567: Someone who can take off, but actually does much better staying on the ground.
Though capable of flight, Archeops was apparently better at hunting on the ground.
568-569: Someone whose release is so sharp it can finish off, in a moment, someone already weak.
The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.
570-571: Someone who attacks those they hate with such fierce bitterness that they hurt themselves too along the way, without thinking about their own safety.
With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.
572-573: Someone something slippery helps dodge every blow, and what makes them slippery is worth a lot of money.
A special oil that seeps through their fur helps them avoid attacks. The oil fetches a high price at market.
574-575-576: Someone who shows people their fate, and whoever is shown vanishes that day, never to be seen again.
A criminal who was shown his fate by a Gothitelle went missing that same day and was never seen again.
577-578-579: Someone of whom it's said that whoever drinks what surrounds them gains wisdom, but it's toxic to everyone but them.

580-581: Someone who starts dancing at nightfall, and whoever dances in the middle is always the group's leader.
Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.
582-583-584: Someone who seems made of two stuck together, and who stays permanently cold.
People believe this Pokémon formed when two Vanillish stuck together. Its body temperature is roughly 21 degrees Fahrenheit.

This Pokémon absolutely loves sweet berries. Sometimes it stuffs its cheeks full of so much food that it can’t fly properly.

Amoonguss generally doesn’t move much. It tends to stand still near Poké Balls that have been dropped on the ground.

The reason it helps Pokémon in a weakened condition is that any Pokémon coming after them may also attack Alomomola.

599-600-601: Someone whose parts all spin fast together, and whose new, sharp part isn't alive at all.
The three gears that compose this Pokémon spin at high speed. Its new spiked gear isn’t a living creature.
602-603-604: Someone who crawls out of their own world, grabs what they want on the shore and drags it straight back in.

Sometimes found drifting above wheat fields, this Pokémon can control the memories of its opponents.

In homes illuminated by Chandelure instead of lights, funerals were a constant occurrence— or so it’s said.

When the weather gets hot, these Pokémon turn into water vapor. Cryogonal are almost never seen during summer.

Discarding its shell made it nimble. To keep itself from dehydrating, it wraps its body in bands of membrane.

For some reason, this Pokémon smiles slightly when it emits a strong electric current from the yellow markings on its body.
619-620: Someone whose kicks are blindingly fast, and one kick of theirs breaks huge rocks into small pieces.
Delivered at blinding speeds, kicks from this Pokémon can shatter massive boulders into tiny pieces.
621: A cruel, cunning person who takes over a home someone else dug and treats it as their own.
Druddigon are vicious and cunning. They take up residence in nests dug out by other Pokémon, treating the stolen nests as their own lairs.
622-623: Someone there's a theory about: that an engine runs inside them that never stops, but no one has proven it yet.
There’s a theory that inside Golurk is a perpetual motion machine that produces limitless energy, but this belief hasn’t been proven.

Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.

These Pokémon live in herds of about 20 individuals. Bouffalant that betray the herd will lose the hair on their heads for some reason.

629-630: Someone who decorates themselves with what others left behind, and has fashions that come and go.

631: Someone whose fiery tongue melts even the hardest armor to get at what's inside.
A flame serves as its tongue, melting through the hard shell of Durant so that Heatmor can devour their insides.
632: Someone who can bite through rock, and works together with others to protect what's dearest to them.
With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.
633-634-635: Someone who attacks from several directions in turns, and doesn't slow down until the other side falls.
The three heads take turns sinking their teeth into the opponent. Their attacks won’t slow until their target goes down.
636-637: Someone who emerged from a cocoon of raging flames, depicted in ancient paintings as a god of fire.
This Pokémon emerges from a cocoon formed of raging flames. Ancient murals depict Volcarona as a deity of fire.
650-651-652: Someone who, in a defensive stance with arms in front of their face, can withstand even an explosion.
When it takes a defensive posture with its fists guarding its face, it could withstand a bomb blast.
653-654-655: Someone who creates a fiery whirlpool by the power of thought, and whoever is swept into it burns.

656-657-658: Someone who appears and vanishes with a ninja's grace, toying with rivals in fast moves and cutting them sharply.

659-660: Someone whose belly keeps warmth exceptionally well, and what they shed was once used by others for winter clothes.
The fur on its belly retains heat exceptionally well. People used to make heavy winter clothing from fur shed by this Pokémon.

Talonflame dives toward prey at speeds of up to 310 mph and assaults them with powerful kicks, giving the prey no chance to escape.
664-665-666: Someone whose pattern changes with the place and climate they grew up in, scattering colors around them.
The patterns on this Pokémon’s wings depend on the climate and topography of its habitat. It scatters colorful scales.
667-668: Someone with enormous destructive power that they choose not to use, preferring things simple and raw.
The temperature of its breath is over 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit, but Pyroar doesn’t use it on its prey. This Pokémon prefers to eat raw meat.
669-670-671: Someone who can live for hundreds of years, and is said to devote their whole life to guarding their garden.
Its life can span several hundred years. It’s said to devote its entire life to protecting gardens.
672-673: Someone who lives up high, and in their group the leader is decided by a head-on clash.
They inhabit mountainous regions. The leader of the herd is decided by a battle of clashing horns.
674-675: Someone who predicts the other side's moves, and strikes with a single blow that can turn a truck into scrap.
Using its leaf, Pangoro can predict the moves of its opponents. It strikes with punches that can turn a dump truck into scrap with just one hit.
676: Someone who just grows wild if left alone, but lets only someone they trust shape them.
Left alone, its fur will grow longer and longer, but it will only allow someone it trusts to cut it.

The defensive instinct of the males is strong. It’s when they’re protecting themselves or their partners that they unleash their full power.
679-680-681: Someone with powers to manipulate others, who once made people build a kingdom exactly the way they wanted.
Its potent spectral powers allow it to manipulate others. It once used its powers to force people and Pokémon to build a kingdom to its liking.

The scents Aromatisse can produce range from sweet smells that bolster allies to foul smells that sap an opponent’s will to fight.
684-685: A soft, sweet person full of air, which is why they're lighter than they look.
Slurpuff’s fur contains a lot of air, making it soft to the touch and lighter than it looks.
686-687: Someone whose hypnotic power is said to have played a part in events that moved history.
It’s said that Malamar’s hypnotic powers played a role in certain history-changing events.
688-689: An extremely alert person who looks in every direction, and in danger acts on pure instinct, almost without thinking, until the rival is defeated.

692-693: Someone whose arm is a cannon, and whose shots can sink even the biggest.
Clawitzer’s right arm is a cannon that launches projectiles made of seawater. Shots from a Clawitzer’s cannon arm can sink a tanker.
694-695: Someone who only needs to sit in the sun and open up to produce enough energy to light up a whole city.
One Heliolisk basking in the sun with its frill outspread is all it would take to produce enough electricity to power a city.
696-697: Someone whose single bite wrecks a car, and who was once the king of an ancient world.
A single bite of Tyrantrum’s massive jaws will demolish a car. This Pokémon was the king of the ancient world.
698-699: Someone who, gripped by rage, gives off a freezing cold that covers everything around them in ice.
When gripped by rage, Aurorus will emanate freezing air, covering everything around it in ice.

It always strikes a pose before going for its finishing move. Sometimes opponents take advantage of that time to counterattack.

Since Dedenne can’t generate much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.
703: Someone of whom it's said that somewhere in the world there are many more like them, sleeping together in a hidden place, with a queen.
It’s said that somewhere in the world, there’s a mineral vein housing a large pack of slumbering Carbink. It’s also said that this pack has a queen.

Small roots that extend from the tips of this Pokémon’s feet can tie into the trees of the forest and give Trevenant control over them.

In the darkness of a new-moon night, Gourgeist will come knocking. Whoever answers the door will be swept off to the afterlife.

725-726-727: Someone whose rudeness and aggression stand out most, but the way they help the little ones reveals a soft side too.
Incineroar’s rough and aggressive behavior is its most notable trait, but the way it helps out small Pokémon shows that it has a kind side as well.
728-729-730: Someone for whom every confrontation is a stage, and whose singing and dancing hypnotize the whole audience.

731-732-733: Someone known for creating harmonious couples, so they're brought to weddings as a good-luck charm.
Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.

Patient by nature, this Pokémon loses control of itself and pounces when it spots its favorite meal—Rattata!
736-737-738: Someone who, carrying a helper that holds spare energy, can fire powerful beams at a rapid pace.

739-740: Someone who starts hitting before stopping to think, and is on record for pushing back a whole avalanche with a barrage of punches.

Ribombee absolutely hate getting wet or rained on. In the cloudy Galar region, they are very seldom seen.

It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.
753-754: Someone with a fine, delicate sharpness who, after collecting enough light, can fire a cutting beam.
The petals on this Pokémon’s arms are thin and super sharp, and they can fire laser beams if Lurantis gathers light first.
755-756: Someone who glows in a dark place and draws people in, but it's best not to get close, because near them you fall into a deep sleep.
If you see a light deep in a forest at night, don’t go near. Shiinotic will make you fall fast asleep.
757-758: Someone in a contest with others like them, where whoever surrounds themselves with the most admirers wins.
The winner of competitions between Salazzle is decided by which one has the most male Salandit with it.
759-760: Someone with moves that would make a martial-arts champion jealous, who hugs tight what they caught and carries it home.
